overview: ALS Limited is an Australian-headquartered global testing, inspection and certification (TIC) company operating more than 450 laboratories and facilities across 70+ countries with over 23,000 employees. The Group provides analytical testing and technical services through two reportable segments — Commodities (mining, mineral, energy and industrial testing) and Life Sciences (environmental, food, pharmaceutical/clinical and consumer products testing) — after restructuring away from a prior three-segment model that also separately reported Industrial. ALS generated underlying revenue of A$3.32 billion in FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026), making it one of the largest listed TIC operators globally behind SGS, Eurofins, Bureau Veritas and Intertek.

business_model.summary: ALS earns fee-for-service revenue by performing scientific testing, sample analysis and certification for clients across mining/exploration, environmental, food, pharmaceutical and industrial end-markets. Revenue is largely transactional/volume-driven (samples processed, tests performed) rather than long-term contracted, though multi-year service relationships with large miners, government environmental programs and pharma clients provide a degree of recurring demand. The business scales through a global 'hub-and-spoke' laboratory network that centralises specialised/high-value testing in hub labs while local spoke labs handle collection, sample prep and routine testing, providing operating leverage as volumes rise.

revenue_streams.name: Commodities (Minerals, Mine Site Production, Industrial Materials incl. Assay & Inspection, Oil & Lubricants, Coal)
Life Sciences (Environmental, Food, Pharmaceutical/Nuvisan, Consumer Products)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — mining companies and exploration juniors, government/environmental agencies, food & beverage manufacturers, pharmaceutical companies and CROs, industrial/oil & gas clients
business_model.geographic_mix: Global footprint across 70+ countries; APAC and EMEA are the largest and most consistently profitable regions for Environmental and Minerals; the Americas (particularly the US, following the York acquisition) has been a source of recent underperformance

competitive_position.market_position: ALS ranks among the top-10 global TIC operators by revenue and is described by industry sources as the fastest-growing major operator (~18% combined organic and acquired growth in FY26), driven by leadership in mineral/exploration testing. It holds the largest market share specifically within global mining and mineral exploration testing, though the broader multi-hundred-billion-dollar TIC market remains fragmented, with the top three global players (SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek) holding only ~23% combined share.

moat_factors.description: Global network of 450+ labs with centralised hub labs for specialised/high-value testing gives ALS capacity flexibility and cost efficiency that smaller regional labs cannot match, particularly in Minerals where it is the largest provider of analytical services to global mining

Testing accuracy underpins client trust (assay results affect mining reserve reporting, drug approvals, food safety compliance); switching away from an accredited, trusted lab carries real risk for clients, creating moderate switching costs
Proprietary high-performance analytical methods, particularly in geochemistry, and a growing base in emerging contaminant testing (PFAS) where ALS has built early leadership
Commodities/Life Sciences mix is intended to smooth earnings — resilient Environmental, Food and Pharma revenue partially offsets the cyclicality of mining exploration testing

weaknesses: Significant earnings sensitivity to mining exploration and junior miner capital-raising activity, a highly cyclical end market
Fragmented, moderately commoditised end markets outside of specialised niches, limiting pricing power in routine testing
Recent acquisition integration issues (York in the US Environmental business) have weighed on segment margins and management credibility on M&A execution
Exposure to a May 2026 cyber security incident highlights operational/IT risk in a business that depends on data integrity and client trust

growth_drivers: Structural growth in mineral exploration and critical minerals demand linked to the energy transition, electrification and AI-driven power/metals demand
Continued build-out of hub laboratory capacity (Lima, Sydney, Bangkok, Prague — ~A$230m committed growth capex) to capture volume growth in Minerals and Environmental
PFAS and emerging microcontaminant testing growing at double-digit (mid-teens) organic rates, now ~6% of Life Sciences revenue, driven by tightening global environmental regulation
Automation, robotics and AI-enabled lab processes expected to deliver productivity gains and margin expansion from FY27 onward
Completed Nuvisan (pharma/CRO) transformation program delivering ~€25 million p.a. run-rate cost savings and a more diversified, less client-concentrated revenue base
Bolt-on M&A in Food, Environmental and Industrial Materials to build regional leadership positions
Ongoing deleveraging (1.5x net debt/EBITDA at FY26 vs 2.3x in FY25) creating balance sheet capacity for further growth investment or M&A

business.description: Minerals/Commodities segment (39% of FY26 revenue, ~64% of segment EBIT) is directly tied to mining exploration and junior miner capital-raising activity; a downturn in commodity prices or exploration budgets would sharply reduce sample volumes and pricing power, as has occurred in prior cycles (e.g., FY2015-2016)

The York (US Environmental) acquisition has underperformed expectations, with progress toward ALS operating standards taking longer than planned; management flagged 'internal operating challenges' in the Americas Environmental business
Environmental division experienced softer trading in the US and Latin America in FY26, contrasting with stronger APAC/EMEA performance
Minerals and Environmental collectively represent 66% of Group revenue, concentrating earnings in cyclically correlated end markets

financial.description: Revenue and costs are earned in AUD, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD and other currencies; FX movements contributed a 1.9% tailwind to FY26 revenue growth and can reverse; USPP debt is issued across multiple currencies to provide a natural hedge

Leverage reduced to 1.5x net debt/EBITDA post the June 2025 equity raise (well within 1.7x-2.3x target range), with 13.5x interest cover and $580m+ available liquidity; USPP notes maturing out to 2034 provide long-dated funding, though bank facilities require periodic refinancing (most recently in May 2026)

financial.risk: Dividend payout sensitivity to earnings cyclicality
financial.description: Payout ratio of ~57% of underlying NPAT means dividends could be cut in a commodities downturn, as occurred historically

regulatory.description: Operations across 70+ jurisdictions carry hazardous waste handling, environmental permitting and anti-bribery/sanctions compliance risk; ALS also holds interests in Russian-based operations that require ongoing sanctions monitoring and potential restructuring/divestment

A May 2026 cyber security incident (post FY26 year-end) involving unauthorised third-party access to IT systems led to a threat actor publishing claimed stolen data; ALS notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre and continues to investigate scope and client/data impacts, with reputational and potential regulatory follow-through risk
ALS is refreshing its climate strategy and target in FY27 amid tightening international climate-reporting regimes

macro.description: Sustained high commodity prices and critical minerals demand have driven the current upcycle; a reversal in mining capex/exploration spending is the single largest swing factor for Group earnings
~10% of drawn debt is floating rate; higher-for-longer rates increase funding costs and can dampen junior miner capital raising, indirectly reducing exploration testing demand
Management flagged an increasing geopolitical risk trend, early logistics/freight disruption, and a specific ~A$5-10 million earnings risk from Middle East-related supply chain disruption for FY27
FY26 commentary noted a US government shutdown, shifting tariff policy and rising gas prices as sources of uncertainty affecting the Americas business

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global TIC market continues to grow structurally on the back of tightening regulation (environmental, food safety, pharma quality), outsourcing trends, and rising demand for specialised testing (PFAS, critical minerals, energy transition materials). ALS-specific Minerals testing is currently in a cyclical upswing supported by high commodity prices and critical minerals demand linked to electrification and AI infrastructure buildout.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High in Commodities/Minerals (correlated with mining exploration capex and junior miner equity raising); low-to-moderate in Life Sciences (Environmental, Food, Pharma testing is more defensive/regulation-driven), giving the blended Group moderate overall cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — ~90% of drawn debt is fixed-rate (3.7%) with long-dated USPP notes to 2034, limiting direct sensitivity; indirect sensitivity via impact of rates on mining exploration financing and junior miner capital raising

recent_developments.event: ALS reported record FY26 results: underlying revenue up 10.7% to A$3.32bn, underlying NPAT up 25.8% to A$381.2m, underlying EBIT up 19.3% to A$599.0m, achieving FY27 strategic targets a year ahead of schedule; final dividend of 23.1 cps declared, full-year dividend up 10.1% to 42.5 cps

Post year-end, ALS disclosed a cyber security incident involving unauthorised third-party access to IT systems, causing temporary operational disruption; a threat actor subsequently claimed to have published data obtained from ALS systems. ALS notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre and does not currently expect a material financial impact, though investigation is ongoing
Refinanced/replaced USD50 million (A$72.8m) bilateral revolving bank facility maturing May 2026, extending weighted average debt maturity to ~4.0 years

H1 FY26 half-year results: underlying revenue up 13.3% to A$1,659.6m, underlying NPAT up 17.2% to A$178.4m; leverage at 1.8x net debt/EBITDA; management highlighted strong Minerals, Industrial Materials and Food growth against softer, historically-pricing-pressured Environmental performance

Completed A$367.4 million equity raise (A$345m Share Placement at $16.70/share plus a Share Purchase Plan at $16.51/share) to reduce debt, fund the ~A$230m organic hub laboratory expansion program, and strengthen the balance sheet
Board renewal: Tonianne Dwyer retired after nine years as Non-Executive Director; Christy Boyce appointed as a new Independent Non-Executive Director
Completion of the two-year Nuvisan (pharma/CRO) transformation program, delivering ~€25 million p.a. annualised cost savings and a 451 bps margin improvement in the segment during FY26
Ongoing integration of the York (US Environmental) acquisition proved more complex than anticipated, weighing on Americas Environmental performance, with leadership changes made in response

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Malcolm Deane and Chairman Nigel Garrard characterised FY26 as a landmark year, having achieved FY27 financial strategy targets (set in 2022) a full year ahead of schedule, driven by resources-sector strength, disciplined cost management and positive pricing. Management flagged the Americas Environmental business (including York integration) as a disappointment requiring continued remediation, and adopted a more cautious near-term view on junior miner exploration conversion (citing an extended lag between capital raising and field activity) alongside an estimated A$5-10 million FY27 earnings risk from Middle East-related supply chain disruption. Management also emphasised that automation, robotics and AI-enabled digital transformation investments are expected to deliver their first tangible productivity/margin returns in FY27.

bull_case: Structural tailwind from critical minerals demand (energy transition, electrification, AI infrastructure) is driving a multi-year mineral exploration upcycle, with Minerals margins above 30% for five consecutive years and still expanding

Diversified Commodities/Life Sciences portfolio smooths cyclicality versus pure-play mining services peers, while PFAS/emerging contaminant testing provides a secular, regulation-driven growth engine within Life Sciences

Balance sheet significantly de-risked post the 2025 equity raise — leverage down to 1.5x net debt/EBITDA, 13.5x interest cover, $580m+ liquidity — providing flexibility for further organic investment or bolt-on M&A
Record FY26 results achieved FY27 strategic targets a year early, evidencing execution strength and giving credibility to continued margin expansion guidance into FY27
Consensus analyst view is constructive (Buy-leaning rating from 14 analysts, average price target meaningfully above recent trading levels), reflecting confidence in the growth and margin trajectory
bear_case: Heavy dependence on the mining exploration cycle means a reversal in commodity prices or a slowdown in junior miner capital raising would sharply compress Minerals volumes, pricing and Group earnings, as has happened in prior downcycles

Recent M&A execution has been mixed — the York (US Environmental) integration has underperformed expectations and management itself called the Americas Environmental result 'a disappointment', raising questions about acquisition discipline

The May 2026 cyber security incident, involving unauthorised access and a threat actor's data leak claims, creates reputational, client-trust and potential regulatory/legal risk in a business whose value proposition rests on data integrity

FY26's strong result was flattered by FX tailwinds (1.9% of revenue growth) and favourable H2 pricing that may not repeat, while management itself guided cautiously on near-term junior miner conversion and flagged a Middle East-linked supply chain earnings risk of A$5-10 million for FY27

Valuation reflects an already-elevated cyclical earnings base (record NPAT, margins at multi-year highs), leaving limited room for further re-rating if the resources cycle or Life Sciences recovery disappoints
